brief: A spending tracker where categories are geological layers — deeper is necessity, surface is discretionary

dominant_strengths: Geological metaphor is executed literally and beautifully — earth-tone gradient from sand to bedrock makes necessity vs discretionary instantly legible
Color palette is cohesive and emotionally evocative; sedimentary stratification doubles as a chart and a concept
Right-rail insights reuse the layer vocabulary (Deepest expense, Avg. depth) reinforcing the system's internal language
dominant_weaknesses: Tooltip overlaps the Sandstone row's percentage and label, occluding data and revealing weak hover-state choreography
Percentages on darker layers (Limestone, Bedrock) have low contrast against the band, hurting scanability of the actual numbers
Typography is competent but generic sans — misses an opportunity for a more editorial or geological character to match the concept
fix_priorities: Reposition tooltip outside the chart bounds or anchor to cursor with offset to prevent occlusion
Increase contrast of percentage labels on dark strata; consider lighter weight in cream tone
Add subtle texture or stratum grain to bands to push the geological metaphor from clever to tactile
Differentiate typography for category names (perhaps a serif) to add reflective weight matching the concept
rationale.norman_balance: Strong visceral and reflective pull from the metaphor, but behavioral utility lags due to tooltip occlusion and weak number contrast.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — the layered stratigraphy directly visualizes necessity-depth, making the brief's metaphor structurally readable rather than decorative.
